title: The Quiet Visitor
premise: Felix Vane, a property surveyor with five years of carefully rationalized noises behind her, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House just as an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside. The house has been waiting for a witness, and Felix's arrival completes a condition the founders never fulfilled: someone must finish the ritual that keeps the thing beneath contained, or it walks free into the town that built its wealth on the bargain. As Felix uncovers the founders' ledgers and her own family's buried complicity, she must choose between loyalty to the people who kept the secret to survive and the truth that the ritual demands a willing keeper. In the end Felix takes the founder's place behind the door — not as a sacrifice, but as a negotiator — sealing herself in with the visitor on terms she writes herself, leaving the house finally, terribly quiet.
about_author: E. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former architectural historian who spent a decade documenting buildings no one wanted to live in. Their fiction has appeared in several small-press horror anthologies, and they write from a house that is, they insist, perfectly ordinary.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Felix Vane arrives at Hollowmere House to conduct a final survey before sale, cataloguing settling cracks, cold rooms, and a staircase that counts wrong. Her POV establishes five years of rationalized noises and a professional armor of measurements. The emotional beat is brittle control — she measures everything because measuring keeps her safe.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Felix documents the house's 'defects' while flashbacks surface the night five years ago she first heard knocking in a wall with no neighbor. The town surveyor, Aldous Reeve, urges her to sign off quickly and leave. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture in her denial, as the house responds to being measured.

chapters.title: The Crew Breaks Ground
chapters.summary: An excavation crew, brought in to assess foundation damage, strikes something beneath the cellar — a stone door, its hinges on the inside. Foreman Dana Okonkwo's POV shows working-class pragmatism curdling into dread as the men refuse the lower level. Emotional beat: collective denial meeting physical proof.

chapters.title: Sealed from Within
chapters.summary: Felix inspects the door and realizes the impossible: the bolts were thrown from the inside, and the stone is warm. That night the knocking resumes — from below, patient, almost polite. Emotional beat: her rationalizations collapse one by one, and she feels, horribly, expected.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Searching the estate records, Felix finds the 1893 ledger of the Hollowmere founding families — seven names, seven signatures, and a recurring entry: 'provisions for the quiet visitor.' Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the realization that the house's wealth was purchased, not earned.

chapters.title: What Dana Saw
chapters.summary: Dana's crew begins quitting; one man, Pell, describes the door breathing when he touched it and won't come back for his tools. Dana, needing the payout, stays. Emotional beat: loyalty to her crew versus the wage that feeds her family — the book's first hard bargain.

chapters.title: Aldous Knows
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Aldous Reeve, whose family name appears in the ledger. He admits the town has renewed the seal every generation and begs her to finish the survey, take the fee, and forget. Emotional beat: fury at a lie of inheritance — and the seductive comfort of being told she can still walk away.

chapters.title: The Visitor's Voice
chapters.summary: Alone at night, Felix hears her own name spoken through the floor in a voice like her late mother's. She answers before she can stop herself. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; the thing below has been studying her for five years, through every house she surveyed.

chapters.title: Seven Names, Six Graves
chapters.summary: Felix and Dana cross-reference the founders against parish records: six founders died in town and were buried; the seventh, Maren Vane, simply vanished — Felix's ancestor. Emotional beat: complicity becomes blood; the debt was always going to come due in her family.

chapters.title: The Ritual of Keeping
chapters.summary: In Maren's hidden papers, Felix finds the ritual: not a banishment but a contract, requiring a keeper of the founder's line to sit with the visitor and renew terms each century. The last renewal lapsed in 1974 — the year the noises began. Emotional beat: dread reframed as duty; the horror has an instruction manual.

chapters.title: Aldous's Confession
chapters.summary: Aldous reveals his father was the last keeper, and that he refused the duty out of resentment, letting it lapse. He has been paying in smaller ways ever since — the town's quiet disappearances. Emotional beat: cowardice exposed; Felix sees her own five years of denial mirrored in him.

chapters.title: The House Turns
chapters.summary: The house begins rearranging itself — doors that open onto 1893, rooms holding the founders' last supper, still warm. Dana, trapped overnight, witnesses a century collapse. Emotional beat: the house stops pretending; it is a machine for making keepers.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: The town council, convened in secret, votes to force Felix into the role by withholding her escape — her car disabled, the roads 'flooded.' Emotional beat: betrayal; the people she'd protect choose her life over her consent, and loyalty curdles into captivity.

chapters.title: Dana's Choice
chapters.summary: Dana, disgusted by the council, smuggles Felix out — but at the town line Felix stops the truck. Below, the visitor's voice is weakening; if it dies unfed, it doesn't vanish, it wakes. Emotional beat: love against duty — Dana begs her to drive; Felix gets out.

chapters.title: Reading Maren
chapters.summary: Felix returns and deciphers Maren's marginalia: the founder didn't sacrifice herself — she negotiated, and the 'ritual' is a conversation the founders were too afraid to hold honestly. Emotional beat: hope inside horror; the door is sealed from the inside because the last keeper locked herself in willingly.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Felix unbolts the door from the outside — the one gesture the ritual never anticipated — and descends. The stair counts true on the way down. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into agency; she goes in as no founder ever did, unarmed and unforced.

chapters.title: The Quiet Visitor
chapters.summary: Face to face at last: the visitor is not a monster but a tenant, ancient and starving, kept by fear because no one ever asked what it wanted. It shows Felix the truth — the founders fed it lies, and it fed the town. Emotional beat: awful empathy; the monster is the most honest character in the book.

chapters.title: New Terms
chapters.summary: Felix drafts a new contract in Maren's ledger: not feeding it people, but feeding it truth — the town's buried crimes, spoken aloud each year, witnessed. The visitor accepts, because it was always starving for witness, not flesh. Emotional beat: the price of survival renegotiated into the price of honesty.

chapters.title: The Council Objects
chapters.summary: Aldous and the council attempt to seal the door with Felix inside on the old terms, preferring a fed monster to a confessed town. Dana and the remaining crew hold the stair. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth — the town fights to keep its own lie alive.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: The house itself intervenes, manifesting the founders' supper one final time and making the council sit through what their ancestors did. Aldous breaks, signs the new terms, and confesses publicly. Emotional beat: catharsis; the truth, once spoken, is the strongest seal.

chapters.title: The First Witnessing
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, the town gathers at Hollowmere and speaks its buried history aloud while Felix, as keeper, carries the ledger down and returns by dawn — the door now open by design. Emotional beat: ritual reborn as reckoning; survival finally has an honest price.

chapters.title: A Perfectly Ordinary House
chapters.summary: Months later, Felix appraises Hollowmere for sale as a home, not a secret. The noises are gone — or rather, answered. Dana helps her pack the last box; the final line notes the staircase counts right, and that Felix has stopped measuring. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace with a door left deliberately ajar.
